summary: (1) Build. `taskset -c 0-11 lake env lean -DwarningAsError=true GX/SingularII/Developing.lean` exits 0 with no output. `taskset -c 0-11 lake build GX` gives 'Build completed successfully (8577 jobs)' with no warnings. grep finds no sorry, admit or axiom in the file. campaign/WP-35d/Axioms.lean, re-run, gives [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound] for singular_manifold_holonomy_indeed_of_isLocallyUnloopable, singular_developing_theorem, existsUnique_holonomy and descend_developing_map. (2) What changed. `git diff` against a57989d (89 lines, +64/-25) shows that no existing Lean statement or proof changed. The diff touches the module docstring (marks, hypothesis checklist, SCOPE (d)) and the docstrings of existsUnique_holonomy, descend_developing_map and singular_developing_theorem, and adds one theorem, singular_manifold_holonomy_indeed_of_isLocallyUnloopable. It proves the same statement as singular_manifold_holonomy_indeed, with reg(M)'s semilocal simple connectedness derived from X locally unloopable through semilocallySimplyConnected_compl_of_sing_subset with S = sing M, which is closed. (3) The four ruled rows, checked against the paper (l.1712 standing 'M, N connected'; l.1660 standing 'X locally unloopable'; §3's l.810 'Hausdorff, LPC, first countable', made binding on §2.5 by DEC-66 (a)). lem:holonomy (l.1753): existsUnique_holonomy takes Γ with [MulAction Γ M], every γ an a.e. morphism A → A, and f : M → X an a.e. morphism, with M connected and locally connected. It concludes ∃! ρ : Γ →* G with f(γ•x) = ρ(γ)•f(x). That is exactly DEC-67 (b). A is any set of charts, which is weaker than the paper's maximal atlas. Connectedness is the l.1712 standing hypothesis, local connectedness is part of being a singular manifold, and faithfulness is part of analyticity and is needed for uniqueness. Closing and marking are correct. rem:singular_manifold_holonomy_indeed (l.1768), under DEC-67 (c): for a developing map D of \widetilde M = MaxBranchedCover (Sing M) y₀ with holonomy ρ, the theorem proves (a) D ∘ ofPoint is IsGXMorphism on the universal cover of reg(M) with its cover structure, which is the classical developing-map predicate of GX.developing_theorem (l.454); and (b) there is a hol : Deck(\widetilde{reg M}/reg M) →* G, equivariant for D ∘ ofPoint, with hol γ = ρ γ' for an extension γ' of γ to \widetilde M. Extensions are unique because ofPoint has dense image in a T2 space, so (b) is 'the holonomy is the restriction'. LPC M (DEC-66 (c)), T2 and first countable M (DEC-66 (a)) and connected M (l.1712) are all ruled. The new corollary uses only the l.1660 standing hypothesis in place of slsc. Closing and marking are correct. lem:descend_developing_map (l.1780): IsQuasiGaloisian p : M → N, B a maximal a.e. atlas on N, with T2 M, T2 N, LPC N and first countable N. These are DEC-66 (a)(c) for the base and Hausdorff for a singular manifold. The theorem proves (∃ D, developing map of p with IsHolonomyOf p D 1) ↔ ∃ a.e. morphism N → X, and adds the factorisation D = D̄ ∘ p. 'The holonomy is trivial' is ρ = 1, which does not depend on D (developing_pair_unique, isHolonomyOf_iff). (ii) ⇒ (i) follows the paper (D̄ ∘ p is invariant). (i) ⇒ (ii) uses lem:dense_orbits through hp.exists_mem_nhds, and the quotient map from cor:spread_connected_image, as the paper does. No extra hypothesis is added. Closing and marking are correct. prop:branched_devmap (l.1807): singular_developing_theorem takes M : Type u with SingularGXStructure, T2, LPC, first countable and connected, plus the l.1660 standing IsLocallyUnloopable X. It proves (i) ∃ developing map of SpreadEnd.base on \widetilde M ↔ (ii) ∃ N : Type u in §3's class (T2, LPC, first countable; DEC-66 (a) covers every space of §3) with a branched covering p and a developing map. The universe restriction on (ii) only weakens the hypothesis side of (ii) ⇒ (i), and exists_developing_maxBranched_of_branchedCovering proves that direction in every universe. The proof route differs from the paper's (SCOPE (c), kept as a finding), but the cited results (universality, the classical developing theorem, lem:dense_orbits analogues) are all built. Closing and marking under DEC-66 (c) are correct. (4) Docstring contract. The four rows are now bold-marked with their rulings cited, and none of them rests on a sorry or on an unruled hypothesis. The hypothesis checklist and SCOPE (a)-(d) match the code. (5) Name clashes. All 19 declaration names checked (the new one included) have 0 definitions outside this file in GX/ or scaffold/. The strict build succeeding also rules out clashes in the import closure. (6) REPORT.json. It is honest for the four dispatched rows: status, decls, hypotheses and build claims all reproduce, including the 8577-job count. It is not complete, as noted below.

issues.where: GX.singular_manifold_holonomy_indeed (and its _of_isLocallyUnloopable corollary), the last conjunct
issues.problem: 'Holonomy the restriction' (DEC-67 (c)) is stated as: for every γ there exists an extension γ' with hol γ = ρ γ'. The statement does not say that γ' is unique, or that γ ↦ γ' is a homomorphism Deck(\widetilde{reg M}/reg M) → Γ(\widetilde M/M). Both are true (ofPoint has dense image and \widetilde M is T2), so nothing is weakened. The 'restriction' map is left implicit.
issues.fix: Optional: add a sentence to SCOPE (d) saying the extension γ' is unique (density of ofPoint, T2), so the conjunct determines hol as ρ composed with the extension map.
